title: Fortran Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none

write(*,'(A)') "Hello, Asha!"
end program lesson
exercises.question: A program block holds the steps. The A format writes character text. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The A format writes character data. The string is sent to the default output unit. implicit none makes you declare variable types instead of guessing them.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: pencils = 3
write(*,'(I0)') pencils + 2
end program lesson
exercises.question: integer declares a whole-number value. The I0 format prints it without leading padding. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The integer variable holds 3. I0 prints the sum 5 without width padding. Declare variables before executable steps.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
real :: length = 2.5
write(*,'(F3.1)') length
end program lesson
exercises.question: real holds a decimal value. The F3.1 format prints one digit after the decimal point. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The real value is 2.5. F3.1 reserves three places with one decimal place. Choose a wider output format for a wider number.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 5, 8]
write(*,'(3(I0,1X))') scores
end program lesson
exercises.question: An array stores several values. This array has three integer positions. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The array has three values. The repeated I0 format prints each whole number. Array sizes and initial value counts must agree.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 5, 8]
write(*,'(I0)') scores(2)
end program lesson
exercises.question: Fortran arrays normally start at position 1. Parentheses select an item. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Fortran starts ordinary array bounds at 1. Position 2 contains 5. Do not assume array indexing starts at zero.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: score = 8
if (score >= 5) then
 write(*,'(A)') "Pass"
else
 write(*,'(A)') "Try again"
end if
end program lesson
exercises.question: An if block runs one branch based on a logical test. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The score is at least 5, so the then branch runs. Close the block with end if.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: n
do n = 1, 3
 write(*,'(I0)') n
end do
end program lesson
exercises.question: A counted do loop includes both its start and end values. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The do counter takes 1, 2 and 3, including both range ends. Do not change the loop counter inside the counted loop.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: values(3) = [2, 3, 4]
write(*,'(I0)') sum(values)
end program lesson
exercises.question: sum adds the values in an array. It is a built-in array operation. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: sum adds 2, 3 and 4 to make 9. sum returns a result; it does not change the array.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer :: scores(3) = [4, 8, 9]
where (scores >= 7) scores = scores + 1
write(*,'(3(I0,1X))') scores
end program lesson
exercises.question: where applies a change only where an array condition is true. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The condition selects the last two positions. Only those values increase, becoming 9 and 10. The mask and array must have compatible shapes.

exercises.code:
program lesson
 implicit none
 write(*,'(I0)') twice(4)
contains
 integer function twice(n) result(answer)
  integer, intent(in) :: n
  answer = n * 2
 end function twice
end program lesson
exercises.question: A function has a result. contains separates the main steps from local function definitions. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: twice takes input 4. Its result variable receives 8. Give the function input and result explicit types.

exercises.code:
program lesson
 implicit none
 integer :: n = 4
 call double_value(n)
 write(*,'(I0)') n
contains
 subroutine double_value(value)
  integer, intent(inout) :: value
  value = value * 2
 end subroutine double_value
end program lesson
exercises.question: A subroutine is called with call. intent(inout) means this input may be changed. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: call passes n as an inout value. The subroutine changes the original to 8. Use call for a subroutine; a function is used in an expression.

exercises.code:
program lesson
  implicit none
integer, allocatable :: scores(:)
allocate(scores(3))
scores = 0
write(*,'(I0)') size(scores)
deallocate(scores)
end program lesson
exercises.question: An allocatable array gets its size when allocate runs. deallocate releases its storage. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: allocate creates three positions. size reads that count before deallocate releases them. Allocate before using the array and do not use it after deallocation.
